he answered:
"It is not fitting for us to give an empty city to our friend."
It is said
that one hundred thousand amphorae {OCR?} were found in one of its storehouses,
and in the library, one million and forty thousand volumes.
And Saladin took these books alone from Amid,
and gave them to al-Qadi al-Fadil,
that is to say, the illustrious judge,
his secretary.
And Saladin confirmed Ibn Qara Arslan with oaths.
And he crossed the Euphrates and went against Aintab;
and there submitted to him Nasih (Nasih,
Nasir) al-Din ibn Kumartakin, its lord.
And he left it and went and encamped against Aleppo and besieged it.
Now Imad al-Din, its lord,
because he had found it empty,
was greatly pressed by his troops to give them provisions (annona).
And he had nothing from within,
nor was anything coming in to him from outside,
because Saladin held the whole country.
For when he said to one of the nobles,
"I have nothing to give you,"
he answered him,
"Sell your wife's jewels and give to the warriors,
if you wish to be king."
And furthermore his situation deteriorated to this point,
that dinner was brought to him every day from the townspeople,
and he and the members of his household ate [it].
And when, for this reason, the nobles and soldiers grew neglectful of fighting,
the townspeople, however, fought very vigorously.
Then Saladin, when he saw that he was not able to take it by fighting,
made a secret pact with the nobles who were inside,
and enticed them with gifts.
And they advised Imad al-Din
that it was better for him to surrender Aleppo,
and take other estates in exchange for it,
and not be negligent until others surrender it,
and he remain empty-handed.
And they said to him further,
"Do you really rely on commoners to fight on your behalf
and eat from their own houses? Behold, their food is exhausted,
and you have nothing to give them.
See now what you will do." And when he yielded to their counsel,
he sent to Saladin,
and asked of him Sinjar, Nisibis, Habur, and Callinicus in exchange for Aleppo.
And Saladin accepted,
and wrote his autograph signature and sent [it] to him,
and also swore to him to give all these things.
